paths.description: Homepage and proxy-entry archetype: first viewport, preferences, responsive layout, metadata, and primary action.
Primary journey: attempt to enter https://example.com and start proxy browsing; the mandatory consent interstitial remained the first blocking state.
Content listing archetype representing proxy-guide navigation.
Long-form article archetype, including raw-HTML discoverability and share metadata.
Primary support form, including labels, autocomplete, and invalid-submit recovery.
Long legal-content template at a narrow viewport.
RTL/localised homepage representative for language, direction, and mobile reflow.
HTTP/error recovery surface using a deliberately unknown route.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to dark or higher-contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: The dark and default screenshots are pixel-identical, the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule, and Lighthouse found 3.02:1 quick-link contrast.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme, provide dark surface/text tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), and add a prefers-contrast/forced-colors treatment.

findings.summary: Page and route changes use abrupt legacy navigation with no modern transition support.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition, animation-timeline, scroll-snap, or related modern interaction declarations across the homepage DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation, preserve reduced-motion fallbacks, and only add declarative motion where it clarifies state.

findings.summary: Long pages and the language menu provide little state-aware navigation guidance.
findings.evidence: The long article and terms captures show static chrome; CSS inspection found no scroll-state, anchor positioning, transition, or attention-highlight support.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight progress/current-location cue on long content and anchor-position the language menu with fallback positions.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent interstitial obscures the page and offers no equal first-layer reject action.
findings.evidence: Fresh-load desktop and mobile screenshots show the primary proxy form dimmed behind a consent dialog describing processing by 210 partners; only Consent and Manage options are offered.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not block core content for non-essential processing. Provide equally prominent Accept and Reject actions, minimise partners/purposes, and retain a clear settings route.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated and several targets are undersized.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports outline-style none for links, the URL input, and buttons; social controls measure 36x32px and many text links are only 17px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring and expand compact controls/links to at least a comfortable 44x44 CSS-pixel hit area without relying on hover.

findings.summary: The mandatory consent wall interrupts the core proxy task before the user can enter a destination.
findings.evidence: The proxy journey screenshot remains at the full-page consent state with the URL field obscured; the initial task cannot begin without accepting or navigating a complex vendor-management flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the proxy input available before optional ad/analytics consent and defer non-essential scripts until an explicit choice.

findings.summary: Mobile lab performance is slow and visually unstable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports Performance 0.87, Speed Index 5.4s, TTI 12.4s, TBT 210ms, and CLS 0.135; the first-party trace still shows LCP 1.71s with no long tasks in that separate run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the main content, reserve late UI space, delay non-essential ad/analytics work, and break/defer interaction work until after the core form is usable.

findings.summary: Third-party and unused JavaScript dominate delivery.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 47 requests and 1.88MB transferred, including 42 third-party requests and 1.80MB third-party bytes. Lighthouse estimates 546KiB unused JavaScript and 44KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Load one analytics configuration only after consent, remove redundant tag-manager/ad bundles, defer optional sharing/feedback code, and split page-specific code.

findings.summary: Quick-link text fails WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies repeated quick-link failures at 3.02:1 (#6a9452 on #e9f0e5), below the expected 4.5:1 for normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a darker green or change the background so normal text reaches at least 4.5:1 in every theme and state.

findings.summary: Focus visibility, landmark structure, and compact targets weaken keyboard and assistive use.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found no visible outline on focusable controls; the DOM probe found no main/nav/header/footer landmarks and multiple 36x32 or 17px-high targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce semantic landmarks, retain logical headings, add :focus-visible styles, and enlarge compact targets while preserving reading order.

findings.summary: The page logs an ad exception and uses deprecated browser APIs.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records an uncaught adsbygoogle error, three deprecation warnings, and three BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix or isolate the ad slot sizing error, update/remove scripts using deprecated storage/ad APIs, and avoid unnecessary no-store responses that block BFCache.

findings.summary: Images lack intrinsic dimensions and responsive delivery.
findings.evidence: Both image audits report missing width/height and srcset; the 700px PNG logo is displayed at 340px and Lighthouse flags the logo as unsized.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width and height (or aspect-ratio), export an SVG/modern raster logo, and provide responsive sources where raster assets vary by density.

findings.summary: Important quick links are not crawlable and indexing signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse finds proxy quick links implemented with data-href rather than href. robots.txt exists, but /sitemap.xml returns the branded not-found page and inspected pages expose no canonical URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href attributes with JS enhancement, publish a valid sitemap, and add self-referencing canonicals plus hreflang across localised variants.

findings.summary: Article pages omit structured data and social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The representative article has a descriptive title and meta description but no JSON-LD and no Open Graph tags.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Article JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching the visible title, description, image, locale, and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Security policy and cookie defaults are weaker than the service promise warrants.
findings.evidence: CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent. Four analytics/consent cookies are not Secure and all seven cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Move to nonce/hash-based CSP, set frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a restrictive Permissions-Policy, and set Secure plus the narrowest viable SameSite/HttpOnly cookie attributes.

findings.summary: The privacy footprint is disproportionate to the simple proxy-entry page.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe sees 13 third-party origins and known Google trackers; HAR attributes 1.80MB of 1.88MB to third parties, while the consent UI describes 210 partners and precise-geolocation use.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to no non-essential collection, reduce vendors and duplicate analytics IDs, batch essential telemetry, and load advertising/sharing only after explicit consent.

findings.summary: Sign-in is password-only and lacks autofill tokens.
findings.evidence: The exercised sign-in modal contains email/password fields with empty autocomplete attributes and no WebAuthn/Passkey capability in the loaded document.
findings.suggestedFix: Add username/current-password tokens immediately and offer passkeys/WebAuthn as the phishing-resistant primary or upgrade path.

findings.summary: Consent choice architecture favours acceptance over refusal.
findings.evidence: The initial dialog offers a one-click Consent button but no equal Reject button, despite listing 210 partners, legitimate-interest processing, and precise geolocation.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer Reject all beside Accept all with equal prominence, use privacy-preserving defaults, and avoid forcing optional consent to reach the primary service.

findings.summary: Account and support inputs omit useful autocomplete assistance.
findings.evidence: Feedback email and sign-in email/password fields all report empty autocomplete values; sign-in is password-only.
findings.suggestedFix: Use email, username, current-password, and relevant support-form autocomplete tokens, then add passkeys and clear account/cancellation controls.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts and media consume most of the page budget without serving the core form.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 96% of transferred bytes to third parties; GTM, Font Awesome, ads, consent, feedback, sharing, and fonts dominate a simple URL-entry page.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a page-weight/third-party budget, remove duplicate analytics and oversized icon libraries, self-host/subset fonts, and defer optional vendors until needed and consented.

findings.summary: The idle memory footprint is heavy for a mostly static entry page.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 461,255 V8 nodes and 29.5MB self size, including 132,916 native nodes and 27,666 closures. Repeating the language toggle did not grow DOM nodes, so this is footprint rather than a demonstrated leak.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant vendor bundles, lazy-load consent/vendor detail UI, and track heap/DOM budgets in repeated-session tests.

taskList.title: Make consent non-blocking, symmetric, and privacy-minimal
Remove duplicate/optional third-party bundles and enforce a page budget
Harden CSP, browser policies, and cookie attributes
Fix contrast, focus visibility, targets, and landmarks
Reserve image/UI space and optimise responsive assets
Repair crawlable links, sitemap, canonical, hreflang, and article metadata
Add autofill tokens and passkey-capable authentication
Add preference-aware theming and restrained modern navigation cues
Set and monitor a proportionate heap/DOM budget
